::: {.lead}
In Lecture 10 you learned frames and the frame rate, resolution and aspect
ratio, containers, codecs and bitrate, and the settings for each target.
Today you use them in a free video editor. There are no new ideas: two
short problems. Do each one alone. The results of the activities are at the
end of this worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- A video is a series of **frames**; the frame rate counts them per
  second. The **resolution** is the size (1920 × 1080), the **aspect
  ratio** the shape (16:9 wide, 9:16 tall).
- The **container** (MP4, MOV) holds the tracks; the **codec** (H.264,
  ProRes) compresses them.
- A higher **bitrate** gives a better picture and a bigger file; too little
  gives blocks in fast action.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1280 × 720|ProRes"}
What is the resolution of Full HD?
:   1920 × 1080

Which codec plays on almost every phone?
:   H.264

A fast chase looks like blocks. What is too low?
:   the bitrate
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · A project with the right settings

A video editor never changes the source files: the **project** keeps the
edits. First set the **resolution** and the **frame rate** of the project
(DaVinci Resolve: File › Project Settings). Then **import** the clips (File
› Import › Media, or drag them): they appear in the **media pool**, where
the clip details show their resolution, frame rate and codec.

![From a new project to an exported file.](images/workflow.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Moving the source files after the import gives "media offline".
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Project and clips · 15 min"}
1. Make a project of 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps. Import three short clips: your
   own phone videos, or the clips your teacher gives.
2. For each clip, write its resolution, frame rate and codec. Which clip
   does not match the project?

*Your product:* a table of three clips and one sentence.

::: {.check}
A typical table: clip 1, 1920 × 1080, 30 fps, H.264; clip 2, 1080 × 1920,
30 fps, H.264 (a tall phone video); clip 3, 1920 × 1080, 60 fps, H.265.
Clip 2 does not match: it is tall in a wide project, so it must be
cropped, not stretched. Clip 3 has twice the frame rate of the project.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The project"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the Deliver page|the clip's name"}
What do you set first in a new project?
:   the resolution and the frame rate

Where do the imported clips appear?
:   the media pool

What happens to the source files when you edit?
:   nothing

A tall phone clip goes into a wide project. What do you do?
:   crop it, never stretch it
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Export for the store

The project is not a video: it must be **exported** (DaVinci Resolve: the
Deliver page). For the store: **MP4**, **H.264**, the resolution and frame
rate of the project, a good quality, and a clear name with a version.

![The export settings.](images/export-settings.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Two exports · 18 min"}
1. Drag your clips onto the timeline in a good order.
2. Export `yourname-teaser-v1.mp4`: MP4, H.264, 1920 × 1080, 30 fps.
3. Export the same project again with a much lower bitrate (or quality):
   `yourname-teaser-low.mp4`. Compare the two file sizes and the moving
   parts of the picture.

*Your product:* two files, their sizes and one sentence.

::: {.check}
A typical result: the v1 file is a few MB for 10–20 seconds and looks
clean; the low-bitrate file is much smaller, and its fast moving parts show
blocks. A higher bitrate gives a better picture and a bigger file. Send the
MP4, never the project file.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Export"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the project file|a GIF"}
Which page of DaVinci Resolve makes the video file?
:   Deliver

Which is a good file name?
:   rooftop-teaser-v1.mp4

What do you send to the producer?
:   the MP4 file

What do you do after the render?
:   watch the whole file once
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. A project is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps. A clip is 1920 × 1080 at 60 fps. Does it match?
2. Why does the editor show "media offline"?
3. Which container and codec do you choose for a store trailer?
4. You export a clip at a much lower bitrate. What happens to the file and the picture?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. No: its frame rate is twice the project's.
2. The source files were moved after the import.
3. MP4 with H.264.
4. The file is smaller, and fast action shows blocks.
:::
